user.title: Load Insights
user.description:
Reads what your Energy dashboard already knows and forecasts consumption from it. Nothing is re-entered here.

Found in the Energy dashboard: {grid} grid, {solar} PV, {battery} battery, {devices} individual devices, {forecasts} PV forecast entries.

data_description.name: Shown as the device that groups the forecast sensors.

data_description.weather_entity: Supplies the coming week's temperatures. Pre-filled when the instance has exactly one weather entity.
data_description.outdoor_temperature_entity: Supplies the past weeks' temperatures from its statistics. Together with the weather entity it lets the forecast respond to cold and hot spells; a sensor whose temperature turns out not to matter for consumption is ignored automatically.

data_description.calendar_entities: Link any calendars. Load Insights works out from past events what each one means for consumption - an away calendar, a bookings calendar - and ignores one that turns out to mean nothing. Event titles are learned separately where they differ from the calendar's average.
data_description.input_entities: Any entity worth trying as an explanation - a tariff block, an electricity price, irradiance, an occupancy sensor. Load Insights works out from its recorded history whether it explains consumption, and ignores it if not. A sensor with few values is used as it is; a numeric one is cut into bands.
data_description.battery_capacity_entity: Optional. A sensor (Wh or kWh) with the battery's usable capacity - for example installed Ah x state of health x nominal voltage from the BMS, so the size follows the pack's ageing. While it reads, it replaces the capacity entered on the Energy dashboard; when it is unavailable, its last reading is kept.

abort.no_energy_dashboard: The Energy dashboard has no grid source configured. Set up at least the grid there first; PV, battery and individual devices improve the forecast.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Load Insights is already set up.

menu_options.input_links: Link an input to what it explains

inputs.title: Explanatory inputs
inputs.description: Inputs the forecast may learn from. Each is kept only if it actually explains consumption.

data_description.weather_entity: Supplies the coming week's temperatures. Pre-filled when the instance has exactly one weather entity.
data_description.outdoor_temperature_entity: Supplies the past weeks' temperatures from its statistics. Together with the weather entity it lets the forecast respond to cold and hot spells; a sensor whose temperature turns out not to matter for consumption is ignored automatically.

data_description.calendar_entities: Link any calendars. Load Insights works out from past events what each one means for consumption - an away calendar, a bookings calendar - and ignores one that turns out to mean nothing. Event titles are learned separately where they differ from the calendar's average.
data_description.input_entities: Any entity worth trying as an explanation - a tariff block, an electricity price, irradiance, an occupancy sensor, a thermostat. Load Insights works out from its recorded history whether it explains consumption, and ignores it if not. A sensor with few values is used as it is; a numeric one is cut into bands. Load detection reads them too: a switch, a thermostat's heating or anything else that goes on and off says when a load runs.
data_description.battery_capacity_entity: Optional. A sensor (Wh or kWh) with the battery's usable capacity - for example installed Ah x state of health x nominal voltage from the BMS, so the size follows the pack's ageing. While it reads, it replaces the capacity entered on the Energy dashboard; when it is unavailable, its last reading is kept.

data_description.forecast_exclude: Dashboard devices to leave out of the house forecast - a car charger, a pump run on demand. The house forecast is built from its parts and these are never added to it: their energy always comes out of the part that holds them, even while they are too young to count as a part. Their own forecasts are unchanged.

detection.title: Detection settings
detection.description:
How load detection behaves. What it watches is no longer asked here: given the grid connection and the inverters, what the house draws is worked out rather than chosen.

{found}

data.meter_wait_s: Wait for slower meters, at most

data_description.meter_wait_s: Detection judges each step at the grid connection once the meters below it have had time to report it - as long as the slowest of them takes to show a step it shares with the grid, learned from those steps - so a step is placed under the meter that took it, never under one that did not change, and the same whether the history is read at once or a minute at a time. Never longer than this: a meter slower than it is judged with what it has said by then. The named loads' live readings lag by the wait, their energy does not; 0 judges every step at once.
data_description.horizon_skip: Detection judges each step at the grid connection once every meter below it has had time to show it. Tick a meter that shows the house's steps slowly - a plug read every half minute, say: it is still read and still places loads, with what it has said by then, but how long it takes no longer holds every other step back. A meter that never shows a step the house's meter shows sets no wait by itself.

data.ignore_meters: Meters to leave out of detection

data_description.single_device: Tick a meter whose readings are one appliance - a plug with only the pump on it, a boiler's own meter. Its readings are that device, so nothing inside it is offered for naming, and it only takes loads on the phases that device uses. Leave circuit meters unticked - a 3EM on a sub-panel, a house circuit: loads are detected inside those. Until this is saved, the meters whose loads are nearly all one are ticked.
data_description.ignore_meters: Tick a meter detection should not read at all, as if it were not on the Energy dashboard: its readings neither place loads nor split steps, and nothing waits for it.

data.autoname_dashboard: Add named loads to the Energy dashboard

data_description.autoname: A fridge or freezer (a compressor cycling) and a heating element that detection is very sure of and has seen on several days are named by themselves - Fridge 1, Heater 1 - and show as detected loads like any you name. A name you give, change or forget always wins and is never made again for a load like it. Off: nothing is named automatically.
data_description.autoname_dashboard: Puts the energy and power of every named load, the ones you named and the ones named automatically, on the Energy dashboard's device list. A renamed load's entry follows the new name. Only the entries added here are ever removed again (when the name goes, or this is turned off); entries you made are never touched, and one you take out is not put back.

naming.title: Name a detected load
naming.description: Detected loads, one page per meter that saw them - the loads under no meter first. Under each: how many loads it has to name, how many more are waiting, and where the meter is. Named loads have a page of their own. Choose *finished* when you are done - that is what rebuilds the entities.

menu_option_descriptions.naming_named: Rename or forget a load you have named.

naming_list.title: {group}
naming_list.description:
Biggest first - {count} of them, {hidden} more than fit here. Click one to see it and give it a name; naming brings you back to this list.

Each row says what a load draws and on which phases, how long a run lasts and what it might be. Under it: what it uses a week and a run, how many times it ran and over how long, when it last ran, when it usually runs, its week from Monday to Sunday, and - if it may be another setting of the same device - what that other load looks like. Give two the SAME name to say they are one device on different settings. Choose *finished* when you are done - that is what rebuilds the entities.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description:
What Load Insights sees right now.

{overview}

reset_detection.title: Reset load detection?
reset_detection.description: The signature library is forgotten and the last ten days of the meter are read again from scratch. Names you have given are kept: each is handed back to whatever the rebuild finds that looks like it, and where nothing matches - which is what a genuinely changed site looks like - the name does not return. It runs on its own and takes a while. Do this after a change to the meter, a rewired phase, or an update that changes how loads are found.

grid.title: Grid connection

data_description.grid_device: Pick it and the per-phase readings are filled in below. Leave empty to choose by hand.
data_description.source_kind: Says what a shortfall at the grid connection is: energy bought from the utility, a generator someone has to start, or - off grid - a load that goes unserved. The forecast's arithmetic is the same either way; this decides how the overview words it.

menu_option_descriptions.naming_name: Type a name to give it entities of its own.
menu_option_descriptions.naming_adopt: The old entry keeps its history but stops carrying the name. Its energy is not added to this one - they are two behaviours of one appliance, not one meter.

naming_name.title: Name this load
naming_name.description:
{row}

Type a name to give it entities of its own. Give two loads the SAME name to say they are one device on different settings. Leave the box empty to go back without changing anything. Tick an input that helped find it to link it to the load - it keeps counting for the whole site as well; the link is made when you finish naming.

data_description.same_as_meter: A device with a meter of its own: pick that meter and the load is named exactly as it is, and is that device - its meter's readings and forecast stand for it, so it gets no detected sensors of its own. Picked, it wins over the name typed above.

inverters.title: Inverters
inverters.description:
One inverter at a time. The house is the sum: the grid meter, plus what each inverter puts OUT less what it takes IN. A PV inverter has no input and contributes its whole output; a hybrid contributes the difference. Nothing needs to be said about how it is wired for this - the sum comes out right either way.

Solar set up here overrides the Energy dashboard's own solar sources, which is what a DC-coupled site needs: arrays charging a battery through MPPTs never appear on the AC side at all.

Leave every power reading empty to remove an inverter.

{found}

data_description.device: Pick it and its readings can be filled in below.
data_description.topology: Parallel: it feeds the bus directly, and its battery, if any, charges from AC. Series: everything flows through it, and its battery sits on the DC bus in front of the conversion.

data_description.power: Use this where the inverter publishes only a total. Per-phase is better where it has it: a cloud then cancels exactly.

data_description.in_power: What the inverter draws from the grid at its own AC input. A PV string inverter has none - leave it empty and it contributes its whole output. A hybrid has one, and the difference is what it actually adds, so the grid it passes through is not counted twice.

naming_waiting.title: Still reading history
naming_waiting.description:
Load detection is working through the recorder - it is {behind}, about {progress}% of the way.

There is nothing to name yet. A library part way through a backfill holds whatever happened in the first few days, and rows that would change under you are worse than no rows.

It keeps going on its own; **Refresh** looks again.

input_links.title: Link an input
input_links.description: Every input counts for the whole site. Link one to the devices it is about as well - the room a fridge stands in, a thermostat's floor temperature - and a number among them sharpens those devices' next six hours from its recent value, and every device they sit inside with them. Pick an input, then what it belongs to.

input_links_to.title: What {input} is about
input_links_to.description: Tick the devices and detected loads {input} says something about. A device inside another counts for both. Untick all to leave it with the site only.

suggested_inputs.title: Suggested inputs
suggested_inputs.description: Sensors in the same area as a device on the Energy dashboard, or as a named load's meter, that are not inputs yet: whether someone is there, and the room's temperature and humidity. Tick the ones worth trying. Each becomes an input for the whole site, linked to that device - and like any input, the forecast keeps it only if it explains something.

plan.title: SOC planning
plan.description: Three sensors plan the battery from the house forecast and the Energy dashboard's sun forecast: the target (room for the strongest stretch), the minimum (cover for the weakest) and the daily excess. Each counts a side at full weight for so many hours, then less per hour, so the far days move it less. Values can be negative; the consumer clamps them.

data_description.plan_days: How far ahead the target and the minimum look, and how many days the daily excess lists.
data_description.plan_production_scale: Share of the Energy dashboard's sun forecast to count on, for all three sensors.
data_description.plan_consumption_scale: Multiplies the house forecast, for all three sensors.

data_description.plan_full_soc: The target counts down from here. Used when no entity below is set or it does not read.
data_description.plan_full_soc_entity: Optional. A number that holds the full level, for example the SOC limit a load manager uses.

data.plan_spread_evenly: Planned with their energy spread evenly

data_description.plan_spread_evenly: Devices whose energy the three planning sensors spread evenly over the horizon instead of where it is forecast - a hot water tank or heater whose boost moves to midday while a dull spell needs it round the clock. Only the planning sensors; their forecasts are unchanged.

heat.title: Heat devices
heat.description: Shadow mode: for each heat pump, or air conditioner or heat pump used as heating, Load Insights works out in which hours the heat would cost the least electricity, and later scores that against what the device really did. Nothing is written to any device. Add one device at a time, or remove the ticked ones. Now: {devices}

data_description.name: What the device is called. Naming one that exists replaces it.
data_description.source: A power sensor (hourly mean) or an energy sensor (hourly change). A counter that only moves once a day, such as MELCloud's, is recognised and its day is spread over the hours - see the plan.
data_description.kind: Sets the default target and how far an hour of heat may be moved: a tank a lot, a floor or a house some, a room little.

data_description.target: Flow, tank or room temperature the device works to. Empty: the kind's default (about 35 for space heating, 50 for hot water, 21 for a room).
data_description.target_entity: Optional. An entity that holds the target and takes over from the number while it reads.
data_description.activity_entity: Optional. A climate, switch or binary sensor that says when the device heats. Used only to place the hours of a device that reports once a day.

data_description.remove: Devices to take off the list.

abort.no_detection: Load detection is not set up: choose the main meter first.
abort.nothing_to_name: Nothing to name yet - no loads have been detected.
abort.no_inputs: No inputs yet - add them on the Explanatory inputs page first.
abort.no_suggestions: Nothing to suggest: no occupancy, presence, motion, temperature or humidity sensor that is not an input yet shares an area with a device on the Energy dashboard or with a named load's meter. Give the devices and sensors areas in Home Assistant and they are matched here.

temperature_pair_incomplete.title: The weather response needs both halves
temperature_pair_incomplete.description: Load Insights has the {have} but not the {missing}. The temperature response is fitted on the sensor's recorded past and applied to the weather entity's coming week, so one without the other can never take effect. Add the missing one under Configure -> Explanatory inputs, or clear both.

no_pv_forecast.title: No PV forecast is linked to the Energy dashboard
no_pv_forecast.description: This site produces PV, but its Energy dashboard has no forecast integration linked to the solar source. The grid forecast therefore predicts a week of sunless days, and its import figures are badly pessimistic. Link one (Solcast, Forecast.Solar and others) to the PV source in Settings -> Dashboards -> Energy.

battery_not_modelled.title: The battery is not being modelled
battery_not_modelled.description: The Energy dashboard has a battery at this site, but not {missing}. Without it the state of charge cannot be forecast, so no SOC forecast sensor is created and the grid forecast is the net BEFORE the battery - it says so in its battery_modelled attribute. Both are optional fields on the battery source in Settings -> Dashboards -> Energy.

no_power_factor.title: Some phases cannot tell a heater from a motor
no_power_factor.description: Load detection has a power reading on phase {phases} but no way to work out a power factor there: that needs the phase's current AND voltage, or a power factor sensor. Watts alone cannot separate a 2 kW heater from a 2 kW motor, so detected loads on those phases get no guess at what they are. Add them under Configure -> Load detection.

detection_found_nothing.title: Load detection has found nothing at all
detection_found_nothing.description: The whole history has been read - {samples} readings - and not one load was found. A meter that never moves is the usual cause: an inverter's AC INPUT reads zero at an off-grid site, for instance, while the loads are all on its output. Point load detection at the reading that carries what the house actually draws, under Configure -> Load detection. Devices with their own meters are unaffected.

devices_without_power.title: Some metered devices cannot be detected
devices_without_power.description: {devices} appear on the Energy dashboard but publish no power reading, only energy. Hourly energy is far too coarse to line up with a load switching on, so these devices cannot locate or name anything in load detection. Their forecasts are unaffected.

house_reading_negative.title: The house reading goes negative
house_reading_negative.description:
What Load Insights works out the house is drawing settles BELOW ZERO on phase {phases} ({watts}) when nothing is running. A house does not draw less than nothing, so the reading is something other than consumption.

Almost always one of two things. Either a grid meter is set as the house reading on **Detection settings** when it belongs on **Grid connection** - many meters report import as negative, and only the grid role applies that polarity. Or an inverter is missing from **Inverters**, so what it generates is never added back and the house appears to shrink as the sun rises.

Detection carries on meanwhile, and everything it finds is unreliable.

energy_dashboard_renamed.title: The Energy dashboard still names renamed entities

confirm.title: Point the Energy dashboard at the new ids

options.parallel: Parallel - inverter feeds the grid bus directly (AC-coupled solar, no battery)
options.series: Series - all power flows through the inverter (hybrid with DC-coupled battery)

options.room: Direct room heating or air conditioner (room temperature)

reset_detection.name: Reset load detection
reset_detection.description: Forget every detected signature and start the meter's backfill again. For when the meter changed, or a phase was rewired, and the library describes a site that no longer exists. Names you have given are kept and handed back to whatever the backfill finds that looks like them - so where the site really has changed, and nothing matches, a name simply does not return - unless you ask for the names to go too.

forget_names.name: Forget the names too
forget_names.description: Drop the names as well as the library, so nothing learned before - not even a name waiting to find its load - carries over. Name the loads anew once the backfill has run.

name_load.name: Name a load
name_load.description: Give a detected load a name by its id - the one each load carries in the diagnostics - or clear it with an empty name. For a load the naming page does not offer yet: it only lists loads that have repeated tightly enough, and a load whose runs vary a lot can wait a long time.

load_id.name: Load
load_id.description: The detected load's family id - the "family" each signature carries in the diagnostics. The name goes to every signature of the family.

meter.name: Meter
meter.description: For a load a meter holding several devices saw - its own detector's id, as the detected loads sensor lists it under that meter (Mansarda's #11). Empty for one the grid saw.

name.name: Name
name.description: What to call it. Loads given the same name are one device. Empty clears the name.

backfill_statistics.name: Rewrite a load's energy history
backfill_statistics.description: Write the hours detection saw of a named load - as far back as it has them, about ten days - over its energy sensor's statistics, hourly and five-minute alike, so the Energy dashboard shows its past, and none of what a detection reset or the sensor's first appearance made of it: Home Assistant counts a reading that appears with days in it, or drops, as that hour's energy. Detection does this by itself every hour, wherever a named load's statistics are off what it credits the load with now. The hours before the ten days stay as recorded, except that a name another name was joined into gains that name's older history, and a load named now the hours it kept from before, once. Running it again writes the same.

name.name: Name
name.description: The named load to rewrite. Empty rewrites every named load.
